key_insight: An asymmetric focal loss markedly improved graph neural network prediction of drug-drug interactions by focusing learning on difficult positive cases.
engineering_relevance: This shows that loss-function design can be as impactful as architecture changes for biomedical graph models, offering a simple, tunable way to reduce missed clinically important interactions.
method: Integrated ClinicalFocal loss into a relation-aware graph convolutional network.
Used molecular fingerprints, physicochemical descriptors, and learned embeddings as inputs.
Compared against binary cross-entropy under identical 5-fold cross-validation settings on TWOSIDES.
evidence_signal: On TWOSIDES, ClinicalFocal improved accuracy (0.699→0.892), F1 (0.700→0.894), AUROC (0.766→0.914), and AUCPR (0.714→0.860), with errors consistently reduced across all five folds.
watch_item: Results come from one benchmark and fixed experimental conditions, so broader generalization to other datasets, label distributions, or deployment settings still needs validation.
paper_title: Asymmetric Focal Loss Improves Graph Neural Network Prediction of Drug-Drug Interactions
